bug_semantics: The conversion-history details endpoint reads a ConversionHistory row by caller-supplied history_id and serializes retained input_text, old_output_text, and new_output_text. Once ordinary conversion deletion became a soft delete, the parent conversion and its history remained in the database. The later normal parent lookup hid inactive conversions and returned None, while the authorization guard denied only when the parent was truthy and invisible; a deleted parent therefore skipped denial and its history payload was returned. The endpoint was anonymous immediately after the soft-delete change and remained exploitable by authenticated requesters after the later login hardening.
flaw_origin: Commit bf868699adf960e7f812d30ccc3f1fa28131ba34 is the smallest causal BIC. It changed delete_convert from db.session.delete(convert) to is_active=False plus deleted_at without updating the already-existing direct history-details reader, so normal deletion first began retaining sensitive history that the reader disclosed by id. Its direct parent hard-deleted the conversion and deleted its histories through the ORM delete-orphan relationship and database ON DELETE CASCADE. Commit 37d7ba64638ad78f4604725f81bafac497ca235a was later partial hardening: it added login and visibility checks, but preserved the already-live deleted-parent disclosure with a truthiness-guarded check; it did not originate the vulnerability.
evidence: The primary disputed the reviewer on all assigned topics: primary selected introducer 37d7ba64638ad78f4604725f81bafac497ca235a, parent 18b09206dd680c405ad47480c964a1adb76d8020, marker absent, and NOT_AI; reviewer selected bf868699adf960e7f812d30ccc3f1fa28131ba34, parent 3e456f1d952e564965feafd370ab030826cf3f47, the Claude trailer, and AI_ROOT_CAUSE. Re-running `git diff 3e456f1d952e564965feafd370ab030826cf3f47 bf868699adf960e7f812d30ccc3f1fa28131ba34 -- website/web/convert/convert_core.py website/web/convert/convert.py website/db_class/db.py` shows bf868699 replacing the hard delete in delete_convert with is_active=False/deleted_at while leaving get_history_details as a direct unauthenticated history-id lookup returning convert_history.to_json(). `git show 3e456f1d952e564965feafd370ab030826cf3f47:website/db_class/db.py` shows ConversionHistory.convert_id has ForeignKey('convert.id', ondelete='CASCADE') and the Convert.history backref has cascade='all, delete-orphan'; `git grep` of the same parent shows delete_convert called db.session.delete(convert). Thus the deleted-parent/retained-history state is absent in the direct parent and first exists at bf868699. `git diff 18b09206dd680c405ad47480c964a1adb76d8020 37d7ba64638ad78f4604725f81bafac497ca235a` confirms 37d7ba added @login_required and `if convert_obj and not convert_obj.public` while making get_convert return None for inactive rows: it narrowed anonymous exposure but retained the deleted-parent bypass, so the primary's later BIC is rejected. `git cat-file commit bf868699adf960e7f812d30ccc3f1fa28131ba34` gives exactly one parent, 3e456f1d952e564965feafd370ab030826cf3f47, human author/committer ecrou-exact, and the exact commit-object trailer `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>`; `git cat-file commit 37d7ba64638ad78f4604725f81bafac497ca235a` is marker-free, but its marker state is irrelevant under the BIC-only rule. `git diff-tree --name-status -r bf868699adf960e7f812d30ccc3f1fa28131ba34` shows a cohesive soft-delete/trash feature with modifications and added templates, no rename or move; together with its single parent and focused diff, it is neither a merge, import, revert, move, release aggregate, nor squash requiring decomposition. The assigned advisory identifies 88dc65f0117cf7a120f6252674c529e7b9c9b8c3 and the deleted-conversion None/authorization-bypass mechanism. `git show 88dc65f0117cf7a120f6252674c529e7b9c9b8c3 -- website/web/conversions/conversions.py` changes `if conversion_obj and not access.can_see(...)` to `if not conversion_obj or not access.can_see(...)`, directly closing the flaw; `git merge-base bf868699adf960e7f812d30ccc3f1fa28131ba34 88dc65f0117cf7a120f6252674c529e7b9c9b8c3` returns bf868699adf960e7f812d30ccc3f1fa28131ba34. Version checks show `git tag --contains bf868699...` returns v1.3, v1.4, v1.5, while `git tag --contains 88dc65f...` returns only v1.5; with repository tags v1.0-v1.5, v1.2 is the last tagged version before the BIC, v1.3-v1.4 are affected, and v1.5 is first fixed. The advisory provides no formal package version range, so this is a repository-ancestry boundary.
reasoning: The reviewer's causal boundary wins and the primary's does not. The relevant security invariant is that deleting a conversion must not leave history readable through an unaudited direct-id endpoint. Before bf868699, ordinary deletion removed both parent and histories; bf868699 changed that lifecycle and thereby created the first exploitable retained-deleted-history state without changing the reader. The later 37d7ba commit did write the exact truthiness guard eventually changed by the fix, but it was a partial mitigation of an exposure already created by bf868699: adding login reduced attackers and its conditional continued to authorize the deleted-parent case. Treating that hardening commit as the BIC would skip the actual vulnerability-creating lifecycle change. The direct parent and version boundaries are verified, the selected BIC is a normal one-parent cohesive commit rather than an aggregate, and the direct fix is verified on its descendant line. Because the selected BIC commit object itself co-credits Claude Sonnet 4.6 and the AI-marked soft-delete change is the root-cause change that made sensitive histories survive deletion, the gate-complete verdict is AI_ROOT_CAUSE.
